sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec: no network, home folder unreadable, one scratch folder writable

tools.name: dependency_group_lookup
tools.description: Lookup a dependency group name and return its parsed dependency data without resolving includes. dependency_groups: mapping of dependency group names to their dependencies, group: the name of the group to lookup.

tools.name: dependency_group_resolve
tools.description:
Resolve a dependency group to a list of requirements.
    
    :param dependency_groups: A mapping of dependency group names to their requirements
    :param group: The name of the group to resolve
    :return: A list of requirement strings
    
    Example: dependency_group_resolve({"dev": ["pytest", {"requests": ">=2.0"}]}, "dev") -> ["pytest", "requests>=2.0"]

tools.name: direct_url_from_dict
tools.description: Create and validate a DirectUrl instance from a JSON dictionary. direct_url_dict: A JSON dictionary representing a direct URL, e.g. {"url": "https://example.com/package.tar.gz"} -> {"url": "https://example.com/package.tar.gz"}.

tools.name: direct_url_to_dict
tools.description:
Convert a DirectUrl instance to a JSON dictionary.
    
    Args:
        url: The direct URL to convert
        generate_legacy_hash: If True, include a legacy `hash` field in
            `archive_info` for backward compatibility with tools that don't
            support the `hashes` field.
        strip_user_password: If True, strip user:password from the URL
            unless it is formed with environment variables as specified in PEP
            610, or it is a safe user:password such as `git`.
    
    Returns:
        A dictionary representation of the DirectUrl instance
    
    Example:
        >>> direct_url_to_dict("https://example.com/package.tar.gz")
        {'url': 'https://example.com/package.tar.gz', 'archive_info': {}}

tools.name: direct_url_validate
tools.description: Validate a DirectUrl instance against the specification. url: The URL of the direct distribution, e.g. 'https://example.com/package.tar.gz' -> None. archive_info: Archive information including hash and dist-info directory, e.g. {'hash': 'sha256=abc123', 'dir_info': {'editable': False}} -> None. dir_info: Directory information including editable flag, e.g. {'editable': True} -> None.

tools.name: marker_evaluate
tools.description: Evaluate a marker expression against an environment. marker: A marker expression to evaluate, e.g. 'python_version >= "3.6"' -> True. environment: Mapping containing keys and values to override the detected environment, e.g. {"python_version": "3.8"}. context: The context in which the marker is evaluated, which influences what marker names are considered valid, e.g. "metadata" (default), "lock_file", or "requirement".

tools.name: marker_evaluate_prepared
tools.description:
Evaluate a marker against the supplied environment.
    
    :param marker: A marker expression to evaluate
    :param environment: The environment to evaluate the marker against, normally from prepare_environment
    :returns: True if the marker matches, otherwise False
    
    >>> from packaging.markers import prepare_environment
    >>> environment = prepare_environment({"sys_platform": "linux"})
    >>> marker_evaluate_prepared("sys_platform == 'linux'", environment)
    True

tools.name: default_marker_environment
tools.description: Return the default marker environment for the current Python process. Returns a dictionary mapping environment marker names to their values, e.g. {'implementation_name': 'cpython'}.

tools.name: metadata_from_raw
tools.description:
Create a Metadata instance from raw metadata.
    
    Args:
        data: Raw metadata to create the Metadata instance from
        validate: Whether to validate the metadata during creation
    
    Returns:
        Dictionary representation of the metadata
    
    Example:
        >>> metadata_from_raw({"Name": "example", "Version": "1.0"})
        {"name": "example", "version": "1.0"}

tools.name: parse_metadata_email
tools.description: Parse a distribution's metadata stored as email headers (e.g. from ``METADATA``). data: Distribution metadata stored as email headers, e.g. 'Name: example\nVersion: 1.0\n' -> {'core': {'name': 'example', 'version': '1.0'}, 'unparsed': {}}.

tools.name: package_is_direct
tools.description: Check if a package is a direct dependency. package: A package entry from a pylock file, e.g. {'name': 'requests', 'version': '2.28.1', 'sdist': False, 'wheels': True} -> False.

tools.name: version_range_empty
tools.description:
Return the empty version range. No version satisfies it. prereleases: Whether prereleases are allowed in the version range.
    
    >>> version_range_empty()
    '!'

tools.name: version_range_full
tools.description: Return the full version range. admit_arbitrary: whether to admit arbitrary strings as versions. prereleases: whether to include prerelease versions. -> string representation of the full version range.

tools.name: version_range_singleton
tools.description: Return a strict singleton version range. version: A PEP 440 compliant version string, e.g. '1.0' -> '[1.0, 1.0]'. prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions.

tools.name: version_range_from_bounds
tools.description: Construct a version range using lower and upper bounds. lower: The lower version bound, or null for no lower bound. upper: The upper version bound, or null for no upper bound. include_lower: Whether to include the lower endpoint. include_upper: Whether to include the upper endpoint. Example: version_range_from_bounds("1.0", "2.0", True, False) -> ">=1.0,<2.0".

tools.name: version_range_intersection
tools.description: Compute the intersection of two version ranges. range1: First version range specifier, range2: Second version range specifier. >>> version_range_intersection('>=1.0', '<2.0') '>=1.0,<2.0'

tools.name: version_range_complement
tools.description: Compute the complement of a version range. version_specifier: A version specifier string (e.g., '>=1.0', '<2.0') -> The complement range as a string.

tools.name: version_range_difference
tools.description:
Compute the difference between two version ranges. range1: First version range specifier, range2: Second version range specifier to subtract from the first.
    
    >>> version_range_difference(">=1.0", ">=2.0")
    '>=1.0,<2.0'

tools.name: version_range_is_subset
tools.description: Check if one version range is a subset of another. range1: The first version range specifier, range2: The second version range specifier to check if range1 is a subset of it. >>> version_range_is_subset('>=1.5,<1.8', '>=1.0,<2.0') True

tools.name: version_range_is_superset
tools.description: Check if one version range is a superset of another. outer_range: A version range specifier string for the outer range, inner_range: A version range specifier string for the inner range.

tools.name: version_range_is_disjoint
tools.description: Check if two version ranges are disjoint. range1: First version range specifier, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0'. range2: Second version range specifier, e.g. '>=2.0,<3.0'. Returns True if the ranges have no versions in common.

tools.name: version_range_filter
tools.description:
Yield items from iterable whose version falls inside the range.
    
    Args:
        range_spec (str): A version range specification compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet
        iterable (list[str]): An iterable of version strings
        prereleases (bool | None, optional): Whether to include pre-release versions; None uses PEP 440 default behavior
        
    Returns:
        list[str]: Items from iterable whose versions fall inside the range
        
    Example:
        >>> version_range_filter(">=1.0,<2.0", ["0.9", "1.5", "2.0"])
        ['1.5']

tools.name: version_range_snap_bounds
tools.description:
Narrow finite bounds of a version range using supplied versions.
    
    The result never adds versions. ``contains`` and ``filter`` give the
    same results for the supplied versions. Pre-release settings and
    ``===`` rules still apply, but do not affect the choice of bounds.
    Unbounded ends and intervals containing no supplied version stay
    unchanged. Calling this again with the same versions leaves the result
    unchanged.
    
    Args:
        range_spec: A version range specifier compatible with PEP 440
        versions: A list of version strings to narrow the bounds of the range
    
    Returns:
        A string representation of the narrowed version range
        
    Example:
        >>> version_range_snap_bounds(">=1.0.0,<3.0.0", ["1.2.0", "2.0.0", "2.5.0"])
        '>=1.2.0,<2.5.0'

tools.name: version_range_is_empty
tools.description: Check if a version range is empty. specifier_set: A specifier set string that defines the version range, e.g. ">=1,<2" -> False. prereleases: Whether to include pre-releases in the range.

tools.name: version_range_contains
tools.description: Check if a version is contained in a version range. range_spec: A version range specifier, e.g. ">=1.0,<2.0". version: The version string to check, e.g. "1.5". prereleases: Whether to match pre-releases. installed: When True, accept a pre-release item even if the range would not otherwise allow it. Example: version_range_contains(">=1.0,<2.0", "1.5") -> True.

tools.name: specifier_contains
tools.description: Check if a version is contained in a specifier. specifier: A version specifier string, e.g., '>=1.2.3'. version: The version string to check against the specifier. prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this Specifier. If None, follows PEP 440 defaults. >>> specifier_contains('>=1.2.3', '1.2.3') True

tools.name: specifier_filter
tools.description:
Filter items in the given iterable, that match the specifier.
    
    :param specifier: A version specifier string
    :param iterable: An iterable that can contain version strings and packaging.version.Version instances
    :param prereleases: Whether or not to allow prereleases in the returned iterator
    
    >>> list(Specifier(">=1.2.3").filter(["1.2", "1.3", "1.5a1"]))
    ['1.3']

tools.name: specifier_set_is_unsatisfiable
tools.description:
Check whether this specifier set can never be satisfied.
    
    Returns True if no version can satisfy all specifiers simultaneously.
    
    Args:
        specifiers (str): A string of version specifiers, e.g., '>=1.0,<2.0'
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if the specifier set is unsatisfiable, False otherwise
        
    Example:
        >>> specifier_set_is_unsatisfiable(">=2.0,<1.0")
        True

tools.name: specifier_set_to_range
tools.description: Convert a specifier set to a version range. specifiers: A string representation of version specifiers, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0' -> '[1.0, 2.0.dev0)'.

tools.name: specifier_set_is_subset
tools.description: Check if one specifier set is a subset of another. subset_specifiers: A string representation of the specifier set to check if it is a subset. superset_specifiers: A string representation of the specifier set to check against. >>> specifier_set_is_subset('>=3.12,<3.13', '>=3.12') True

tools.name: specifier_set_is_superset
tools.description:
Check if one specifier set is a superset of another.
    
    Args:
        superset_specifiers: A string representation of the superset specifier set
        subset_specifiers: A string representation of the subset specifier set
    
    Returns:
        True if superset_specifiers is a superset of subset_specifiers, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> specifier_set_is_superset(">=3.12", ">=3.12,<3.13")
        True

tools.name: specifier_set_is_disjoint
tools.description: Check if two specifier sets are disjoint. specifiers1: A string of version specifiers for the first set, specifiers2: A string of version specifiers for the second set. >>> specifier_set_is_disjoint('<3.12', '>=3.12') True

tools.name: specifier_set_contains
tools.description: Check if a version is contained in a specifier set. specifier_set: A string representing the specifier set (e.g., '>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1'), version: The version string to check for containment, prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this SpecifierSet.

tools.name: tag_interpreter
tools.description: Get the interpreter name from a tag triple. interpreter: the interpreter name like 'cp39', abi: the ABI tag like 'cp39', platform: the platform tag like 'linux_x86_64' -> the interpreter name e.g. 'cp39'.

tools.name: tag_abi
tools.description: Get the ABI from a tag. interpreter: The interpreter identifier, e.g. 'cp39'. abi: The ABI identifier, e.g. 'cp39'. platform: The platform identifier, e.g. 'linux_x86_64'. Example: tag_abi('cp39', 'cp39', 'linux_x86_64') -> 'cp39'.

tools.name: tag_platform
tools.description: Get the platform from a tag. interpreter: The interpreter name and version, e.g. 'cp39'. abi: The ABI identifier, e.g. 'cp39'. platform: The platform identifier, e.g. 'linux_x86_64'. Example: tag_platform('cp39', 'cp39', 'linux_x86_64') -> 'linux_x86_64'.

tools.name: interpreter_abi
tools.description: Get the ABI tag of the running interpreter. Returns a string like 'cp312' for CPython 3.12.

tools.name: interpreter_name
tools.description: Get the name of the running interpreter. Returns a string identifier for the current Python implementation, such as 'cp' for CPython or 'pp' for PyPy.

tools.name: interpreter_version
tools.description: Get the version of the running interpreter. warn: Whether warnings should be logged. e.g. '311' -> '311'.

tools.name: parse_tag
tools.description: Parse a tag string into a frozenset of Tag instances. tag: The tag to parse, e.g. "py3-none-any". validate_order: Check whether compressed tag set components are in sorted order. limit: The maximum number of tags to parse. -> frozenset of tag strings in format "interpreter-abi-platform".

tools.name: platform_tags
tools.description: Yields the platform tags for the running interpreter. e.g. ['macosx_11_0_arm64', 'macosx_10_16_arm64']
